**Finding: COMPLIANT** (sits at/above the fallback; no redline proposed)

**Why this deal doesn't fail the rule.** The WARRANTY rule is written for services/software procurement, but this is a drug research, development and commercialization collaboration. Mapping the rule's material terms onto the actual bargain, every element the rule protects is present:

| Rule element | Where it lives |
|---|---|
| Workmanlike / industry-standard performance | §§ 4.2(b), 5.2(b) — all Research and Development activities "in compliance with all Applicable Law (including GMP, GLP and GCP)" plus diligent efforts against Plan timelines. GMP/GLP/GCP *is* the industry standard here. |
| Real remedy | §§ 4.2(b), 5.2(b) cure mechanic (JRDC/JSC-specified cure actions + cure periods) → Sanofi step-in rights, expressly "without prejudice to any other rights or remedies… at law or in equity"; plus RevMed warranty-breach indemnity (§ 14) and termination for material breach. Stronger than the rule's repair/replace/refund floor. |
| Compliance with laws | § 13.2(u) warranty and § 13.4(b) mutual covenant. |
| Disclaimer doesn't swallow the warranty | § 13.5 opens "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY STATED IN THIS ARTICLE XIII," preserving RevMed's 21 express warranties in § 13.2 (ownership free of liens, right to grant, non-infringement, patent validity, no litigation, no government-funding encumbrance, diligence completeness). |
| Product conformance | § 7.3 routes it to the Supply Agreement and Quality Agreement, which "shall cover the documentation and other quality requirements for the acceptance of previously manufactured supply of Product." |

Critically, the walk-away trigger — "AS IS" with everything disclaimed — is squarely avoided. § 13.5 is a conventional carved-out implied-warranty disclaimer, not a swallowing clause.

**Noted, not flagged** (per the playbook's treatment of minor sub-elements):
- No fixed 12-month/90-day conformance-to-documentation period with an express refund election, and no malicious-code warranty. Neither maps to this deal — there is no software or discrete deliverable, and batch conformance is deliberately deferred to the Supply/Quality Agreements.
- § 13.2 warranties are given only as of the Execution Date. Standard for this transaction type, and supplemented by the forward-looking covenants in §§ 13.3–13.4.

**Two items to carry forward into the § 7.3 negotiations** (rather than redline now): secure an express batch conformance warranty (GMP, specifications, no adulteration) with replacement-or-refund remedies in the Supply/Quality Agreements, and confirm § 13.5 is not read to reach warranties given in those Ancillary Agreements — the § 13.5 carve-out is drafted by reference to "this Article XIII" only, so a conformance warranty sitting in a separate Ancillary Agreement should be expressly preserved there.

Redlining Article XIII to bolt on a 90-day deliverable warranty would import procurement concepts that don't fit a collaboration and would reopen a well-balanced warranty package — disproportionate given the bargain already clears the fallback.
